notes: muse's `!` bang shell-escape (live-confirmed: `!echo hello_shell_escape` runs locally, exit 0, ~66ms, zero model call). Every escape-related record is Skip=true at every level of parser.go's dispatch (route()'s top-level default for user_shell.command/user_shell.result; parseRunEvent's default for the escape's own run_id, which only ever carries event.kind:task_stream_linked, never started/terminal; parseSessionEnvelope's default for the kind:task/tool.shell lifecycle) -- live-verified against a real probe transcript that the escape's run_id never receives started/terminal. So the session stays ready throughout the escape window (shell_escape_window), then a trailing real prompt proves the session is still alive with a genuine ready->working->ready arc on a DIFFERENT run_id. Single-birth FilesUnderRoot adapter (session id = directory basename), so session_birth anchors to start UNPINNED, following the 2-1_basic-turn / 2-5_synchronous-slash-command sibling template. CONFIRMED BY RECORDING: session 01a0a13e-dd94-7f00-a979-06f980ac7e39 born ready at T+0, stayed ready until the real 'alive' prompt's forced ready->working at T+8.7s (shell_escape_window duration >=4000ms satisfied; the shell-escape's own transcript growth never sets LastEventType, per forceReadyToWorkingIfActive's guard in session_detector_activity.go, so it cannot itself force a bounce), then working->ready at T+15.9s when the real turn completed. pid_bind now pinned same_session_as:session_birth (was unpinned in the assessed spec -- a latent risk per #1960 shared-context fact 1, not observed misfiring this run since the parent's own pid_discovered landed first, but pinned defensively). CORRECTED pre-promote: dropped the teardown/process_exited phase. Two independent, cited reasons: (1) the daemon reproduced #1962 (processlifecycle's per-PID watched map is last-write-wins) -- the single process_exited event in this recording landed on a reminder-subagent session (ccfe5f58-...), never on the parent 01a0a13e, exactly the fleet-wide pattern already fixed in 2-13_turn-end-terminal-text's and 2-16_oversized-transcript-line's specs; (2) the recipe's own exit_clean step never ran: the driver's step_send increments EXPECTED_TURNS on EVERY send including the shell-escape's, so step_wait_turn's second call waits for turn_count>=2 while the escape produces no turn at all (turn_count tops out at 1) -- it burns the full 120s timeout_seconds budget and then `wait_turn) step_wait_turn || break` exits the script loop before reaching exit_clean, so the muse process was torn down forcibly (tmux/pty teardown), not via a graceful /exit. This second finding is a genuine driver turn-accounting defect specific to any recipe mixing a non-turn send (shell/slash) with a real send before a wait_turn -- worth a future driver fix (step_send should not blindly count every send toward EXPECTED_TURNS), but out of scope for this record pass per the 'don't tune a recipe until it goes green' rule; noted here for the next person touching turn-count.sh.
